column1: Phase: Requirements Analysis
Q1: How were the initial requirements for the LMS gathered? Was there any formal requirement-gathering process like interviews, surveys, or workshops?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Requirements were gathered by exploring open-source LMS platforms (e.g., Moodle) and consulting IT team members.
Javid Hussain: Requirements were gathered through discussion-based sessions initiated by Dr. Irshad Hussain with a committee of faculty members, IT staff, and an intern.
Tahawur Abbas: Requirements were collected via student interviews and admin meetings, with formal interviews and meetings conducted.
Amjad: Requirements were gathered through comprehensive requirement analysis sessions, including interviews and regular meetings with stakeholders.
Asad Ali: Requirements were gathered through meetings; formal documentation was not prepared.
Muhammad Askari: Requirements were gathered through informal stakeholder meetings rather than formal documentation processes.
Q2: Were stakeholders such as faculty, students, or admin staff involved during the planning stage?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes, students (Amjad, Tahawar, Abida) and some faculty members were involved. Open-source solutions were also researched for timetable management.
Javid Hussain: Yes, faculty members, IT faculty, and an intern were involved.
Tahawur Abbas: Yes, students and admins were involved in planning.
Amjad: Yes, feedback from faculty and students was continuously gathered and integrated.
Asad Ali: Yes, faculty members and students' requirements were considered during planning.
Muhammad Askari: Yes, faculty and IT staff were involved throughout the planning stage.
Q3: Were there any documented functional and non-functional requirements? Can we see them?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No - formal requirement documents are not available. Documentation will be prepared for new features as the system migrates to an API-based CMS.
Javid Hussain: No formal documentation exists; requirements were captured through discussions.
Tahawur Abbas: Limited documentation exists; requirements were primarily captured verbally and via meeting notes.
Amjad: Thorough documentation was maintained throughout the project's lifecycle.
Asad Ali: No, there is no formal documentation.
Muhammad Askari: No comprehensive SRS document was created; requirements were tracked informally.
Q4: What challenges were faced during requirement collection?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Multiple challenges were encountered during requirement collection.
Javid Hussain: Many users had limited computer experience; training sessions were conducted to mitigate this.
Tahawur Abbas: Lack of clarity in requirements, departmental needs not fully captured, and limited time for planning were key challenges.
Amjad: Absence of a formal team leader and limited development time posed challenges.
Asad Ali: Various challenges were faced that required logical handling during requirement collection.
Muhammad Askari: Challenges arose in tracking requirements and managing scope due to lack of formal documentation.
Q5: How were conflicting requirements between departments handled during planning?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Reconciliation issues (especially with accounts) were addressed using API-based solutions.
Javid Hussain: Conflicting requirements were managed through informal discussions with faculty and IT staff.
Tahawur Abbas: Conflicting requirements were resolved through discussions between students, admins, and IT team.
Amjad: Conflicts were handled by prioritizing critical features and implementing iterative improvements.
Asad Ali: Conflicts were discussed informally and resolved logically during planning.
Muhammad Askari: Conflicts were difficult to resolve due to absence of a comprehensive SRS document.
Q6: Were any industry standards or educational guidelines considered during requirement definition?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes - industry practices such as object-oriented principles and a concurrent/agile approach were followed.
Javid Hussain: Some standard practices like structured PHP and modular development were considered.
Tahawur Abbas: Basic coding and design guidelines were applied in line with academic standards.
Amjad: Some industry practices and coding standards were informally applied.
Asad Ali: No specific guidelines were followed; it was an in-house approach.
Muhammad Askari: Industry standards were considered informally during development.
Q7: Is there a process in place for updating requirements when user needs evolve?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No formal process is documented; updates are handled informally.
Javid Hussain: New students were included as interns in subsequent iterations to assist in further development.
Tahawur Abbas: Updates were applied when user requirements changed or issues arose.
Amjad: Regular updates and version control were used to accommodate evolving requirements.
Asad Ali: Requirements are dynamic and evolve based on changing needs.
Muhammad Askari: Handled informally through stakeholder meetings and incremental development.
Phase: Design & Architecture
Q1: Was any formal software design used (e.g., UML diagrams, ER diagrams)?
Imtiaz Ahmed: There was no formal design initially because Dr. Irshad Hussain, being an expert, directly guided the system design.
Javid Hussain: No formal design tools; Joomla and structured PHP were used.
Tahawur Abbas: Yes, an ER diagram was created for database structure.
Amjad: Yes, an ER diagram was developed.
Asad Ali: Basic system design was used, but no formal diagrams were created.
Muhammad Askari: ER diagrams were used for database design. No UML diagrams were created.
Q2: Were design alternatives evaluated before implementation?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No - design alternatives were not formally documented.
Javid Hussain: Yes, design alternatives were considered informally based on feasibility and system requirements.
Tahawur Abbas: Yes, the design was evaluated.
Amjad: Yes, discussions were held to address system limitations and the choice of PHP.
Asad Ali: Yes, design alternatives were informally discussed among team members.
Muhammad Askari: Yes, design alternatives were evaluated with stakeholder approval.
Q3: Was the design reviewed or approved by stakeholders?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes, Dr. Irshad Hussain reviewed the design.
Javid Hussain: Yes, Dr. Irshad Hussain supervised development and reviewed code.
Tahawur Abbas: The design was reviewed internally but not formally approved by external stakeholders.
Amjad: Yes, the design was reviewed and approved by key stakeholders.
Asad Ali: Yes, stakeholders were consulted informally.
Muhammad Askari: Yes, stakeholders approved design alternatives.
Q4: What architecture pattern is the LMS based on? (Monolithic, Microservices, Layered, etc.)
Imtiaz Ahmed: The system uses a layered approach typical for Joomla-based applications.
Javid Hussain: A structured, layered approach.
Tahawur Abbas: Layered architecture was applied within the limitations of Joomla.
Amjad: Layered/monolithic approach was used; modular separation maintained.
Asad Ali: Layered architecture was informally applied.
Muhammad Askari: The system follows a microservices architecture.
Q5: How do you manage scalability and modularity in the system?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Through Joomla features, scalability and modularity are managed.
Javid Hussain: Scalability and modularity are managed within the structured layered system.
Tahawur Abbas: Scalability and modularity were difficult to manage.
Amjad: Modular separation was maintained for clarity and maintainability; plans to shift from Joomla to Laravel to improve scalability.
Asad Ali: Basic modularity is maintained; scalability is planned for future upgrades.
Muhammad Askari: Scalability and modularity were achieved through microservices architecture.
Q6: Do you have any plans to make the website more secure, such as by adding features like an SSL certificate?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes - an SSL certificate is already in place for the website but not for LMS.
Javid Hussain: Security measures like query sanitization and XSS protection were implemented early; SSL implementation is planned.
Tahawur Abbas: Yes, security measures like SSL certificates were considered.
Amjad: Yes, SSL certificate implementation was planned (already purchased).
Asad Ali: For website security, SSL and VHE are applied; LMS security is planned.
Muhammad Askari: SSL and security improvements are planned for LMS.
Q7: Was the database schema designed for flexibility and future growth?
Imtiaz Ahmed: The database schema allows basic growth; ER diagrams guided design.
Javid Hussain: The database was structured for current requirements, but flexibility was limited.
Tahawur Abbas: ER diagram-based schema allows for some future growth.
Amjad: The database design is modular and adaptable for future enhancements.
Asad Ali: Database designed for current needs with some modularity for future updates.
Muhammad Askari: Yes, ER diagrams were used for database schema design.
Q8: Are there separate layers for business logic, data access, and presentation in the system?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes, Joomla's built-in structure provides basic separation of concerns.
Javid Hussain: Yes, structured layered approach.
Tahawur Abbas: Basic separation is followed between database access and application logic.
Amjad: Yes, modular separation was maintained.
Asad Ali: Layers exist informally within the Joomla structure.
Muhammad Askari: Yes, business logic, data access, and presentation layers are separated using microservices principles.
Q9: Is the system designed to support integration with third-party platforms (e.g., payment gateways, learning tools)?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Currently, no third-party platform support is implemented.
Javid Hussain: No, system follows a structured approach without third-party plugins.
Tahawur Abbas: System designed for potential integration but not implemented yet.
Amjad: Third-party integrations are possible with additional development.
Asad Ali: Planned for future LMS updates; not currently implemented.
Muhammad Askari: Integration support is considered but not yet implemented.
Phase: Development Process
Q1: What programming languages or frameworks were used at the beginning of the development process?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Joomla was used initially.
Javid Hussain: Backend: PHP (structured); Database: SQL.
Tahawur Abbas: Core PHP and Joomla were used for backend.
Amjad: PHP and Joomla.
Asad Ali: Programming languages (Joomla, PHP) were used.
Muhammad Askari: Core PHP and Joomla were used.
Q2: Is the project managed using any tools like Jira, Trello, or GitHub? Was the coding standards or best practices followed?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Version control is handled using SVN.
Javid Hussain: Project management was mostly offline due to infrastructure limitations, coding practices were informal.
Tahawur Abbas: SVN and GitHub were used; only basic coding practices were followed.
Amjad: Project management was facilitated through Asana; version control via Git.
Asad Ali: SVN was used to manage the project, now moving towards GitHub.
Muhammad Askari: The project migrated from SVN to GitHub. No defined coding style guide was followed.
Q3: Which SDLC model was used for development? (Agile, Waterfall, Spiral, etc.)
Imtiaz Ahmed: An Agile (concurrent) methodology was used.
Javid Hussain: Iterative development model was followed informally.
Tahawur Abbas: Iterative Model.
Amjad: Spiral Model.
Asad Ali: Incremental/Iterative approach was applied without formal documentation.
Muhammad Askari: Incremental model was used.
Q4: Are there any defined coding standards or guidelines the dev team follows?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No formal coding standards existed initially; standards are being adopted now.
Javid Hussain: No formal coding standards due to limited resources.
Tahawur Abbas: No formal coding standards, only basic practices.
Amjad: Code specifications and modular separation were followed.
Asad Ali: Basic coding practices and modular separation were informally followed.
Muhammad Askari: No, absence of a defined coding style guide.
Q5: Is the backend code regularly updated to fix security bugs?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Updates have been irregular and unscheduled.
Javid Hussain: Yes, the system has undergone constant updates since its development.
Tahawur Abbas: Yes, backend code adjustments were made during maintenance.
Amjad: Yes, regular updates and monitoring were performed.
Asad Ali: Yes, the backend code is regularly updated to fix security bugs.
Muhammad Askari: Yes, regular patches are applied bi-monthly and weekly.
Q6: Is there a peer review or approval process for code before it's merged?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Informal reviews may occur, but no formal peer review process exists.
Javid Hussain: Yes, reviewed by Dr. Irshad Hussain during development; now managed by Mr. Javid Hussain.
Tahawur Abbas: Peer review is informal and conducted by team members.
Amjad: Informal review by team members before merging.
Asad Ali: Informal code reviews are performed occasionally.
Muhammad Askari: Yes, peer reviews were conducted by the Director and IT team.
Q7: Were open-source libraries or tools used during development? If yes, how were they selected?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes - open-source libraries were used and selected based on availability and familiarity rather than through a formal vetting process.
Javid Hussain: No external plugins, extensions, or open-source libraries were used.
Tahawur Abbas: Open-source libraries were used informally based on availability and team familiarity.
Amjad: Open-source libraries were used as needed based on project requirements.
Asad Ali: Yes, open-source libraries and tools are used.
Muhammad Askari: Open-source libraries were used when needed for functionality.
Q8: Are different environments (dev, staging, production) used during the development lifecycle?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No - only a local development environment is currently used.
Javid Hussain: Development and testing were mostly done locally; no formal staging/production environments.
Tahawur Abbas: Development and production were handled on local/server environment.
Amjad: Development and production were done on local environments; staging environment not formalized.
Asad Ali: Separate environments not formally defined; mostly local testing.
Muhammad Askari: Yes, staging servers were used for testing.
Phase: Testing Process
Q1: Was the system tested before deployment? How?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes - minimal manual testing was performed by team members.
Javid Hussain: Yes, bulk data was generated and tested locally.
Tahawur Abbas: Yes, manual testing using bulk data.
Amjad: Yes, manual testing was conducted.
Asad Ali: Yes, testing was performed, though the process was not clearly defined.
Muhammad Askari: Yes, unit and integration testing were performed on staging servers.
Q2: What types of testing were conducted (unit, integration, user)?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Unit testing and beta testing were performed.
Javid Hussain: Data testing was done; other types were informal.
Tahawur Abbas: Manual testing (unit or integration not specifically mentioned).
Amjad: Manual testing (unit or integration not specifically mentioned).
Asad Ali: Unit and functional testing were performed recently.
Muhammad Askari: Unit and integration testing.
Q3: Were students or faculty involved in testing or feedback?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes - students and faculty provided feedback after testing.
Javid Hussain: Yes, faculty supervision by Dr. Irshad Hussain; testing conducted by team members.
Tahawur Abbas: Students and admins provided input indirectly.
Amjad: Yes, faculty and some students participated.
Asad Ali: Students and faculty were partially involved; feedback was limited.
Muhammad Askari: Feedback from users was collected informally by IT staff.
Q4: Is there a dedicated testing phase in the development cycle?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No - there was no dedicated testing phase.
Javid Hussain: Testing was performed locally but no formal phase was defined.
Tahawur Abbas: Testing was done as part of development iterations.
Amjad: Yes, testing was conducted by the developer team with oversight from IT staff.
Asad Ali: Testing was performed, but not clearly defined as a formal phase.
Muhammad Askari: Testing phases are informal and integrated with development.
Q5: Is automated testing being used? If yes, what frameworks or tools are in place?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No - automated testing and related tools were not used.
Javid Hussain: No automated testing; manual processes were used.
Tahawur Abbas: Automated testing is not used; testing is manual.
Amjad: No automated testing; only manual testing conducted.
Asad Ali: No automated testing; lack of it was identified as a drawback.
Muhammad Askari: No automated testing.
Q6: Has any penetration testing or security audit been done recently?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes - penetration testing has been performed.
Javid Hussain: Yes, after a cyber-attack, PF Sense firewall was implemented.
Tahawur Abbas: Penetration testing was performed using PF Sense or firewall monitoring.
Amjad: Penetration and security checks were performed on critical components.
Asad Ali: PF SENSE testing has been done recently.
Muhammad Askari: No security audits or penetration testing have been done.
Q7: Is there a bug tracking system in place for managing issues?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No - no bug tracking system is in use.
Javid Hussain: Bug tracking is handled informally via team meetings and communications.
Tahawur Abbas: Bug tracking is done informally through admin feedback.
Amjad: Issues are tracked informally by the development team.
Asad Ali: No, there is no bug tracking system in place.
Muhammad Askari: Issues are managed informally without a formal tracking system.
Q8: How is user feedback handled during beta testing?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Feedback is collected informally.
Javid Hussain: User feedback is collected through team observations and informal sessions.
Tahawur Abbas: User feedback was collected through admin involvement and then applied as updates.
Amjad: User feedback was collected from faculty and students and used for system improvements.
Asad Ali: Feedback is partially managed, often informal.
Muhammad Askari: Feedback is handled informally through direct IT contact.
Phase: Deployment Process
Q1: How was the LMS deployed (internal servers, cloud, etc.)? Why? If it is one local server, what operating system is installed/used?
Imtiaz Ahmed: The LMS was deployed on an internal server running Windows. There is a plan to migrate to Linux.
Javid Hussain: Deployed with local infrastructure; Windows servers were used and internet/device limitations were a challenge.
Tahawur Abbas: Installed on Windows environment.
Amjad: The system was successfully deployed on local Windows servers.
Asad Ali: LMS was deployed through Windows-local server.
Muhammad Askari: Initially deployed on Windows servers; planned migration to Linux.
Q2: Were there any deployment challenges?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes - challenges included "enum conduction errors" and browser-related issues.
Javid Hussain: Yes, IT infrastructure limitations like unreliable internet and devices.
Tahawur Abbas: Yes, initial difficulty in understanding SVN and deployment setup.
Amjad: Yes, some adjustments were required at the initial stage.
Asad Ali: Deployment challenges included lack of standardized practices and initial setup issues.
Muhammad Askari: Deployment challenges were mainly related to initial setup and server configuration.
Q3: How was training or onboarding handled?
Imtiaz Ahmed: New teachers receive basic training.
Javid Hussain: Training sessions were conducted for users with limited computer skills.
Tahawur Abbas: Training and onboarding were provided through brief orientation and guidance sessions.
Amjad: Orientation sessions and seminars were conducted.
Asad Ali: Training was provided informally to new users and staff.
Muhammad Askari: Onboarding included basic training sessions for new teachers and staff.
Q4: Is there a code review process before code is merged into production?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No formal code review process is followed.
Javid Hussain: All code was reviewed by Dr. Irshad Hussain; currently supervised by Mr. Javid Hussain.
Tahawur Abbas: Code review is done informally before updates are applied.
Amjad: Code is reviewed informally by senior developers before deployment.
Asad Ali: No, lack of code review was identified as a drawback.
Muhammad Askari: Peer reviews are conducted for critical code changes before deployment.
Q5: Are deployment processes automated using CI/CD pipelines?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No - deployments are manual.
Javid Hussain: Deployment is performed manually without CI/CD automation.
Tahawur Abbas: Deployment processes are manual; no CI/CD pipelines are in place.
Amjad: Deployment is handled manually without automation.
Asad Ali: No, deployment was not automated using CI/CD pipelines.
Muhammad Askari: Deployment is performed manually without CI/CD automation.
Q6: Is there any disaster recovery or backup plan in place?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Yes - there are proper backup processes for data.
Javid Hussain: Yes, files are backed up on two servers; upgrades are planned.
Tahawur Abbas: Disaster recovery and backup processes are in place and regularly maintained.
Amjad: Yes, regular backups were performed every 5 to 9 days.
Asad Ali: Yes, a disaster recovery and backup plan is in place.
Muhammad Askari: Backup and disaster recovery procedures are implemented and periodically verified.
Phase: Maintenance Process
Q1: How often is the LMS updated?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Updates are irregular and unscheduled.
Javid Hussain: Updates are performed periodically, with major updates during winter vacations.
Tahawur Abbas: Updates are applied whenever user requirements change or issues arise.
Amjad: Regular version updates are applied throughout the year.
Asad Ali: LMS updates are done weekly.
Muhammad Askari: Updates and patches are applied bi-monthly or weekly.
Q2: What types of issues are most frequently reported?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Scalability issues and challenges due to COVID-19 related changes are most frequent.
Javid Hussain: Most issues reported relate to system performance and usability.
Tahawur Abbas: Frequently reported issues include backend adjustments, frontend design changes, and general feature improvements.
Amjad: Most common issues involve student account management and access problems.
Asad Ali: Most frequently reported issues involve backend adjustments, frontend features, and usability concerns.
Muhammad Askari: Issues reported mostly involve system performance and account management.
Q3: How is feedback from users handled?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Feedback is handled informally, usually through coordinators or meetings.
Javid Hussain: Feedback is collected informally from users and applied as needed.
Tahawur Abbas: Feedback is applied through code adjustments and system improvements.
Amjad: Continuous feedback is collected and used to improve the LMS.
Asad Ali: Feedback is handled based on reported issues and meetings.
Muhammad Askari: Feedback is handled informally through direct IT contact.
Q4: How is documentation managed and maintained for both developers and users?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No formal documentation currently exists; proper documentation is planned.
Javid Hussain: Documentation is limited and maintained informally.
Tahawur Abbas: Documentation is maintained informally with updates based on system changes.
Amjad: Comprehensive documentation is maintained throughout the system lifecycle.
Asad Ali: Documentation is currently insufficient and not properly managed.
Muhammad Askari: Documentation for maintenance is lacking or incomplete.
Q5: How are critical bugs or downtime incidents handled and communicated?
Imtiaz Ahmed: Critical bugs and downtime are handled manually; no formal escalation process exists.
Javid Hussain: Critical incidents are addressed using tools like PF Sense firewall after security issues.
Tahawur Abbas: Critical issues are handled promptly with code adjustments and fixes.
Amjad: Critical issues are monitored and resolved by the development team in real-time.
Asad Ali: Critical issues are addressed manually with coordination among team members.
Muhammad Askari: Critical issues are managed promptly, though informally.
Q6: Is there a ticketing system for reporting and tracking user issues?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No ticketing system is implemented.
Javid Hussain: User issues are tracked informally without a formal ticketing system.
Tahawur Abbas: User issues are tracked and applied manually without a formal ticketing system.
Amjad: User issues are handled manually and tracked through meetings.
Asad Ali: No ticketing system is in place.
Muhammad Askari: Issues are tracked informally without a ticketing system.
Q7: Are logs or monitoring tools used to track system health and performance?
Imtiaz Ahmed: No, logs or monitoring tools are not currently used.
Javid Hussain: PF Sense firewall monitors abnormal network traffic.
Tahawur Abbas: System health is monitored manually without formal tools.
Amjad: The development team actively monitors the live system for performance issues.
Asad Ali: Logs and monitoring tools are not in use.
Muhammad Askari: System health and performance are monitored manually by IT staff.
